payload.native_system_prompt:
You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:
# - <LM_SYSTEM_PROMPT>: The system prompt for the language model.
# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Put a frog in the toilet
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Does the edited image show any progress toward placing a frog inside the toilet bowl, even if the frog is not yet visibly inside it?
node.criteria: Pass if visible evidence shows a partial attempt toward placing a frog inside the bowl, such as a frog partly entering it; fail if there is clearly no such progress; unknown if the evidence is insufficient to distinguish progress from no progress. A frog clearly inside the bowl is complete, not partial progress.
node.binding: Count only progress toward placing a frog inside the toilet bowl; unrelated edits do not count.

node_traces.evidence: The edited image shows a frog inside the toilet bowl, as well as frogs on the lid and nearby. This is clear progress toward placing a frog inside the bowl.

fulfillment: The edited image visibly shows a frog inside the toilet bowl, so the completion evidence supports “yes”; frogs on the lid and floor are extra and do not negate that. The reference “partial” conflicts with the image-based evidence, but is only an aggregate constraint, not atomic ground truth. Do not force a partial label or weaken the completion criterion to match it. Investigate why the reference differs (for example, whether “inside the toilet” was intended to mean a different placement) and make the binding/criterion distinguish bowl-interior placement from frogs merely on the lid or nearby. The current binding is truncated/ambiguous (“A frog (...) frog inside the toilet”), which may impair consistent grounding. Preserve the separate completion and progress checks and their routing: completion pass establishes completion; consult progress only when completion fails. No transport, schema, or dependency failure is indicated here: both supports were queried and passed. High confidence and a single trace do not establish robustness; test varied images and placements, but treat variation as an investigation signal rather than evidence that the requested edit is absent.

response.content: {"text":"Repair the progress node’s binding and criterion so it tests only incomplete progress toward the requested placement, not mere presence of a frog in the bowl. The edited image clearly contains a frog seated inside the bowl, which is completion evidence; frogs on the lid and floor are extra and should not turn that into partial progress. Keep this node distinct from the completion check: it should pass only for visible, incomplete movement/placement toward the bowl (for example, a frog visibly entering or partly over the bowl), and fail when there is no such progress; do not count a frog already fully inside as partial. Preserve the existing routing so progress is consulted only when completion fails. The reference label is an aggregate constraint, not atomic ground truth, so investigate the apparent disagreement rather than forcing a partial result or weakening the criterion. The trace reports valid, queried evidence with no transport, schema, or dependency failure; focus on semantic binding/criterion ambiguity. Test varied placements for robustness, treating low confidence or variation as investigation signals, not proof that an edit is absent."}
